node-2.label: 49-year-old male was admitted in July 2010 due to sudden onset of weakness in the proximal muscles of his limbs, affecting both sensory and motor functions

node-3.label: Clinical examination showed proximal muscle weakness in both upper and lower limbs, tingling and pain, and reduced muscle stretch reflexes in the lower limbs

node-4.label: There were no signs of upper motor neuron involvement

node-5.label: Nerve conduction studies showed normal results

attrs.why: New needle EMG shows abnormal spontaneous activity and neurogenic recruitment, which expert analyses interpret as refuting acquired myopathy. The myopathy hypothesis is downgraded, though not fully excluded because muscle biopsy and aldolase data remain unavailable. Confidence decreased from 0.5 to 0.2.

Needle EMG neurogenic recruitment, together with acute symmetric sensory-motor deficits and hyporeflexia, favors Guillain-Barré syndrome despite normal nerve conduction studies. Experts now regard GBS as the leading diagnosis. Confidence increased from 0.35 to 0.65.

Needle EMG neurogenic pattern argues against a neuromuscular junction disorder, while sensory tingling/pain and hyporeflexia remain atypical. Expert analyses consider NMJ unlikely. Confidence decreased from 0.15 to 0.1.
